title: 2 Things You Didn't Know About the Bugatti Chiron

scenes.text: The Bugatti Chiron has one thousand four hundred seventy-nine horsepower. It cost two point four million euros before options. And almost everything people repeat about it is the boring part. Today we are going to show you two things about the Chiron that most people have never heard, and the second one changes how you see the whole car.
scenes.caption: 2 THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW

scenes.text: Here is a hint. The first secret is hidden in a key. Not the key that starts the car, a second one. The second secret is about heat. This engine throws away more energy as heat than it ever sends to the wheels. And the way Bugatti solved that problem is one of the wildest pieces of engineering ever put in a road car.
scenes.caption: A SECOND KEY?

scenes.text: Along the way you will see the record that a former Formula One driver set without wearing a helmet, the one-off Chiron that sold for almost ten million euros, and the moment in twenty twenty-six when Bugatti changed owners. Every number in this video comes from a published source, and the list is in the description.
scenes.caption: EVERY NUMBER IS SOURCED

scenes.text: But first, to understand why these two secrets exist at all, you need to know what the Chiron had to beat. And the car it had to beat was another Bugatti.
scenes.caption: IT HAD TO BEAT A BUGATTI

scenes.text: The story starts with Ferdinand Piech, the engineer who ran the Volkswagen Group. Around nineteen ninety-seven, riding a Japanese express train, he sketched an eighteen-cylinder engine on an envelope. A year later, in nineteen ninety-eight, Volkswagen bought the Bugatti name. It reportedly paid around fifty million dollars, and it got only the trademark. The old factory and the parts were already gone.
scenes.caption: A SKETCH ON A TRAIN
scenes.chapter: The car it had to beat

scenes.text: Several concept cars followed. One of them, shown at the Frankfurt Motor Show in nineteen ninety-nine, was called the eighteen slash three Chiron. So the name Chiron was used by Bugatti long before the car you know. Then, at the Geneva show in two thousand, Piech promised a car with more than one thousand horsepower and a top speed above four hundred kilometers per hour.
scenes.caption: THE FIRST CHIRON WAS A CONCEPT

scenes.text: That promise became the Veyron. The engine lost two cylinders along the way and became the famous eight-liter W16 with four turbochargers. The Veyron made the dream real. But according to analysts at Sanford C. Bernstein, quoted by evo magazine in twenty thirteen, Volkswagen lost about three point nine million pounds on every Veyron it sold.
scenes.caption: A LOSS ON EVERY CAR

scenes.text: And the Veyron set a very high bar. In twenty ten, a Veyron sixteen point four Super Sport reached four hundred thirty-one kilometers per hour. Whatever came next had to be faster, more powerful, and still usable every day. That is a brutal brief for any engineer.
scenes.caption: 431 KM/H IN 2010

scenes.text: The answer was shown on the first of March, twenty sixteen, at the Geneva Motor Show. It was named after Louis Chiron, a racing driver from Monaco who drove for Bugatti in its golden era. The design team was led by Achim Anscheidt. And the base price was two point four million euros, with a deposit of two hundred thousand euros just to get in line.
scenes.caption: GENEVA, MARCH 1, 2016

scenes.text: The numbers were enormous. Bugatti rated the engine at fifteen hundred metric horsepower, which is one thousand four hundred seventy-nine horsepower, with one thousand six hundred newton meters of torque from two thousand to six thousand r p m. Zero to one hundred kilometers per hour took two point four seconds, and zero to three hundred took thirteen point six.
scenes.caption: 1,479 HP, 1,600 NM

scenes.text: The car was also heavy. Wikipedia lists an estimated curb weight of almost two thousand kilograms, close to forty-four hundred pounds. All-wheel drive, a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox, and a carbon fiber body. Bugatti planned to build only five hundred of them. And here is where our first secret comes in.
scenes.caption: ONLY 500 WOULD BE BUILT

scenes.text: Secret number one. A normal Chiron cannot reach its top speed. Not without help. The car is electronically limited to about three hundred seventy-five to three hundred eighty kilometers per hour in normal driving. To go faster, the driver has to use a special speed key.
scenes.caption: SECRET 1: THE SPEED KEY

scenes.text: With that key in place, the Chiron enters what Bugatti calls Top Speed mode. The car lowers itself, the aerodynamics change, and the limit rises to four hundred twenty kilometers per hour. That is two hundred sixty-one miles per hour. And it is still a limit, not the maximum the car could do.
scenes.caption: LIMITED TO 261 MPH

scenes.text: So why limit a car that cost millions? The main reason given is the tires. At those speeds, every tire is spinning thousands of times per minute, and the forces on the rubber are extreme. Bugatti decided the safe ceiling for a road car on road tires was four hundred twenty kilometers per hour. The key is basically a promise that you really mean it.
scenes.caption: THE LIMIT IS THE TIRES

scenes.text: But here is the twist. Many people believe the famous three hundred and four mile per hour run was done in a Chiron like the ones customers drive. It was not. That car was a pre-production Chiron Super Sport three hundred plus, and it was built for one job.
scenes.caption: IT WAS NOT A NORMAL CHIRON

scenes.text: On the second of August, twenty nineteen, at the Volkswagen Group test track at Ehra-Lessien in Germany, Le Mans winner Andy Wallace drove that car to four hundred ninety point four eight four kilometers per hour. That is three hundred four point seven seven three miles per hour. It was the first time a near-production car went past three hundred miles per hour, and the run was verified by T U V.
scenes.caption: 304.773 MPH

scenes.text: According to Autocar, the record car had an extra safety cell, aerodynamic changes designed with Dallara, a longer tail, a taller seventh gear, and an engine tune of one thousand five hundred seventy-eight horsepower. Its Michelin tires were specially built, and every single one was X-rayed before the run. At top speed each tire turned about four thousand one hundred times per minute.
scenes.caption: EVERY TIRE WAS X-RAYED

scenes.text: Wallace later described the strangest feeling at three hundred miles per hour. It was not the noise or the wind. It was the gyroscopic effect of the spinning wheels, which he felt through the steering. At that speed, the wheels themselves fight to keep going straight.
scenes.caption: THE WHEELS FIGHT BACK

scenes.text: And then Bugatti did something no one expected. The same year, company president Stephan Winkelmann said the goal had been to be the first manufacturer to reach three hundred miles per hour, and that Bugatti would now focus on other areas. In other words, the fastest brand in the world announced it would stop chasing top speed records.
scenes.caption: BUGATTI QUIT SPEED RECORDS

scenes.text: So the production Super Sport three hundred plus was sold with a limit too. Only thirty were made, priced at three point five million euros before tax, and customer cars are limited to four hundred forty kilometers per hour. Even the car named after the record cannot legally repeat the record. That is secret number one. The fastest Chiron is always held back.
scenes.caption: ONLY 30 WERE MADE

scenes.text: Before secret number two, there is another record most people forget. In August twenty seventeen, before the three hundred mile per hour run, Bugatti wanted to prove that the Chiron could not only go fast but also stop. The test was zero to four hundred kilometers per hour, and back to zero.
scenes.caption: 0-400-0 KM/H

scenes.text: The driver was Juan Pablo Montoya. He won the Monaco Grand Prix in Formula One, the Indianapolis five hundred twice, and the twenty-four hours of Daytona three times. And according to Bugatti's own press release, he did this run without a racing suit, without a helmet, and without a HANS device.
scenes.caption: NO HELMET

scenes.text: The Chiron reached four hundred kilometers per hour in thirty-two point six seconds, covering two thousand six hundred twenty-one meters. Then it braked to a full stop in about nine point three seconds and four hundred ninety-one meters. The total was forty-one point nine six seconds, certified by S G S T U V Saar.
scenes.caption: 41.96 SECONDS

scenes.text: The braking part is just as wild. The rear wing turned into an air brake at forty-nine degrees, less than a second after braking began. Bugatti said it added about nine hundred kilograms of downforce at the rear. The car slowed at about two g. And Montoya said the Chiron was really impressive in how stable and consistent it was.
scenes.caption: THE WING BECOMES A BRAKE

scenes.text: But here is the twist. That record did not last. Koenigsegg later beat it, first with the Regera, and then with the Jesko Absolut, which brought the time down to around twenty-five seconds in twenty twenty-five. So the Chiron's first great record is now a reference point for its rivals, not the top of the list.
scenes.caption: THE RECORD DID NOT LAST

scenes.text: Now, secret number two. And this is the one that changes how you see the car. The Chiron's engine produces about fifteen hundred horsepower. But according to Bugatti, as reported by Motor Authority, the engine generates more than three thousand horsepower worth of heat. Twice as much energy is thrown away as heat as is used to move the car.
scenes.caption: SECRET 2: 3,000 HP OF HEAT

scenes.text: That is not a flaw that only Bugatti has. Every gasoline engine turns a large share of its fuel into heat instead of motion. The difference is scale. When your engine makes fifteen hundred horsepower, the heat it throws away is enough to cook the car from the inside if it is not removed every second.
scenes.caption: EVERY ENGINE WASTES HEAT

scenes.text: So Bugatti built a cooling system that sounds like it belongs in a power plant. The Chiron has ten radiators. They cool the engine, the charge air, the engine oil, the transmission, the rear differential, and the hydraulic oil.
scenes.caption: 10 RADIATORS

scenes.text: The water pump moves about eight hundred liters of coolant per minute through the engine. The high-temperature loop holds thirty-seven liters of coolant, and it circulates through the loop in about three seconds. A second, low-temperature loop with twelve liters keeps the charge air from overheating, even in stop-and-go traffic.
scenes.caption: 800 LITERS PER MINUTE

scenes.text: Then there is the air. More than sixty thousand liters of air pass through the engine every minute at full power. The big intakes on the sides, just behind the doors, feed that engine. And under the car, a flat floor with strakes, active diffusers, and NACA ducts pulls cool air across the drivetrain.
scenes.caption: 60,000 LITERS OF AIR A MINUTE

scenes.text: The fuel side is just as extreme. The engine uses duplex fuel injection with thirty-two injectors, two per cylinder. And the official mixed fuel consumption is twenty-two point five liters per one hundred kilometers, which is about ten and a half miles per gallon, and that is the gentle, everyday figure.
scenes.caption: 32 FUEL INJECTORS

scenes.text: The exhaust is titanium. There are four pre-catalytic converters and two main catalysts, and one of them is described as about six times the size of a normal car's catalytic converter. The titanium silencer weighs only about forty-four pounds. And the car has six tailpipes, four at the back and two pointing down.
scenes.caption: SIX TAILPIPES

scenes.text: Even the turbocharging is designed around this problem. The Chiron uses two-stage turbocharging. Two turbochargers work from launch, and the other two join in at about three thousand eight hundred r p m. That is how the car delivers peak torque from two thousand all the way to six thousand r p m, without the huge lag of four big turbos at once.
scenes.caption: TWO TURBOS, THEN FOUR

scenes.text: So here is the real secret of the Chiron. Its greatest achievement is not making fifteen hundred horsepower. Plenty of tuners can make big power for a few seconds. Its achievement is surviving fifteen hundred horsepower, all day, at four hundred kilometers per hour, with air conditioning on and a warranty attached.
scenes.caption: THE REAL ACHIEVEMENT

scenes.text: And that also explains a detail people often miss. The Chiron uses the same displacement and the same number of turbochargers as the Veyron. Motor Authority says the power gain of about twenty-five percent came mainly from more boost and bigger turbos. Almost every part of the engine was redesigned to survive it, with titanium and carbon fiber parts to save weight.
scenes.caption: SAME SIZE, 25% MORE POWER

scenes.text: All of that engineering has a price, and it does not stop at the dealer. Collector Steve Hamilton showed his Chiron maintenance costs on video, and The Drive summarized them in January twenty twenty-three. A normal annual service was about eleven thousand five hundred dollars.
scenes.caption: $11,500 A YEAR

scenes.text: The four-year major service was about thirty-four thousand dollars, which was covered by warranty in his case. An extra four-year bumper-to-bumper warranty was listed at two hundred four thousand dollars. And a single taillight was quoted at more than ten thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: $10,000 TAILLIGHT

scenes.text: The bigger parts are even more extreme. The Drive listed a replacement engine at about eight hundred fifty-six thousand dollars, and a dual-clutch gearbox at about one hundred eighty-five thousand dollars. Front brake rotors were more than eighteen thousand dollars, and front pads around six thousand seven hundred.
scenes.caption: $856,000 ENGINE

scenes.text: But here is a twist about tires. The Veyron was famous for tire sets that cost around thirty thousand to forty-two thousand dollars, and the Veyron's tires had to be replaced every two thousand five hundred miles. For the Chiron, Bugatti engineers said they moved to a standard rim design and a standard mounting process, so the tires are much cheaper and can be changed far more easily.
scenes.caption: THE TIRES GOT CHEAPER

scenes.text: So the Chiron was not only built to be faster than the Veyron. It was also built to fix some of the Veyron's ownership headaches. It is still one of the most expensive cars on earth to keep, but in some areas it is less punishing than the car it replaced. We break down the full ownership cost in a separate video.
scenes.caption: LESS PUNISHING THAN A VEYRON

scenes.text: Now, five hundred Chirons sounds simple. It is not. Inside that number there are many very different cars. The base Chiron accounts for about two hundred. Then there is the Chiron Sport, about sixty cars, a sharper version that is eighteen kilograms lighter and has torque vectoring.
scenes.caption: 500 CARS, MANY VERSIONS

scenes.text: There is the Pur Sport, about sixty cars, built for corners rather than top speed, about fifty kilograms lighter with a higher redline. There is the Super Sport, about eighty cars, with a longer tail and a top speed limit of four hundred forty kilometers per hour. And there are small series like the Chiron Noire and the Les Legendes du Ciel, built in batches of about twenty.
scenes.caption: PUR SPORT AND SUPER SPORT

scenes.text: And then there are the one-offs. One of them, the Chiron Profilee, was built as a single car. In February twenty twenty-three, RM Sotheby's sold it in Paris for nine million seven hundred ninety-two thousand five hundred euros. Hagerty reported that it became the most valuable new car ever sold at auction, far above its estimate.
scenes.caption: €9.79 MILLION

scenes.text: Bugatti also built other cars on the Chiron's foundations, like the Divo, the Centodieci, the Bolide track car, and the open Mistral. They are not counted as Chirons, but they share its heart. In other words, the W16 lived on in many forms after the base car was sold out.
scenes.caption: MORE CARS ON THE SAME HEART

scenes.text: And here is a twist about value. In November twenty seventeen, just months after the first deliveries, evo reported that a used Chiron with about one thousand three hundred thirty miles was offered for three point six million pounds, against a price of about two point five million pounds. The first used Chiron was being sold for more than new.
scenes.caption: USED, FOR MORE THAN NEW

scenes.text: Bugatti sold out the Chiron by January twenty twenty-two. The last base-spec car was built in September twenty twenty-three. And in May twenty twenty-four, the five hundredth and final Chiron left Molsheim. It was a Super Sport called L'Ultime, painted in two shades of blue to recall the very first Chiron of twenty sixteen.
scenes.caption: THE 500TH CHIRON

scenes.text: Top Gear reported that its livery carries place names from the Chiron's story. Geneva, where it was launched. Ehra-Lessien, where it broke three hundred miles per hour. Molsheim, its home. And the number five hundred appears under the rear wing, on the wheel caps, and engraved on the engine cover.
scenes.caption: A CAR THAT TELLS ITS STORY

scenes.text: One more detail people love. In twenty eighteen, Lego and Bugatti built a full-size, drivable Chiron out of Lego Technic. It used more than one million pieces and two thousand three hundred four Power Functions motors. It produced an estimated five point four horsepower and reached about twenty kilometers per hour.
scenes.caption: 1 MILLION LEGO PIECES

scenes.text: And there was a smaller one for everyone else, the Technic set forty-two zero eighty-three, at one to eight scale with about three thousand six hundred parts. For many people, that box is the only Chiron they will ever own. It is a reminder of what the car really became. Not just a machine, but a symbol.
scenes.caption: THE CHIRON MOST PEOPLE OWN

scenes.text: So what replaced it? In June twenty twenty-four, Bugatti revealed the Tourbillon. It drops the quad-turbo W16 for a naturally aspirated eight point three liter V16 developed with Cosworth, plus three electric motors. Total output is about one thousand seven hundred seventy-five horsepower, and the price is about three point eight million euros before taxes.
scenes.caption: THE TOURBILLON

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The Tourbillon is a hybrid, but its top speed is listed at two hundred seventy-seven miles per hour, faster than a normal Chiron's limit. So even the successor was designed around a top speed figure, years after Bugatti said it would stop chasing records.
scenes.caption: 277 MPH HYBRID

scenes.text: And the company itself changed. In twenty twenty-one, Volkswagen moved Bugatti into a new venture with the Croatian electric car maker Rimac, with Porsche holding a large minority stake. Then, in September twenty twenty-six, Carscoops reported that a group of investors bought Porsche's stakes. Volkswagen and Porsche now own nothing of Bugatti, and Mate Rimac became Bugatti's president.
scenes.caption: VW NO LONGER OWNS BUGATTI

scenes.text: Think about that. The Chiron was born inside Volkswagen, from a sketch by Ferdinand Piech. Its successor will be sold by a company that Volkswagen no longer owns at all. The Chiron is the last Bugatti of the Volkswagen era with the original W16 formula as its main car.
scenes.caption: THE END OF AN ERA

scenes.text: So let's recap the two things most people don't know about the Bugatti Chiron. Number one. A normal Chiron is always held back. It needs a special key to reach its limited top speed, and even the three hundred mile per hour record car was a special build. Customer cars never got to repeat it.
scenes.caption: 1. ALWAYS HELD BACK

scenes.text: Number two. The real engineering story is heat, not horsepower. An engine that makes about fifteen hundred horsepower while generating more than three thousand horsepower of heat, cooled by ten radiators, eight hundred liters of coolant per minute, and sixty thousand liters of air per minute.
scenes.caption: 2. A WAR AGAINST HEAT

scenes.text: Those two facts explain the whole car. Bugatti did not build a car that was simply powerful. It built a car that could control that power and survive it, and then it chose to limit it. That is why the Chiron feels different from a dragster or a tuner car with big numbers.
scenes.caption: POWER YOU CAN SURVIVE

scenes.text: Tomorrow we look at the Chiron from three more angles. How it really compares with its fiercest rival, the Koenigsegg Jesko. What it really costs to own one. And the full story behind the car. If you liked this one, the others go deeper.
scenes.caption: 3 MORE ANGLES

scenes.text: Tell us in the comments which secret surprised you more, the key or the heat. And if you are shopping for something a little more practical than a Bugatti, our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description.
